title: Installing mixed PowerToys versions leaves old files

judgment.rationale: Draft PR #49996 provides concrete existing coverage by replacing custom manifest copy/delete behavior with MSI DuplicateFile authoring, but the issue explicitly records unresolved locked-file preflight, reboot replacement, and post-install verification requirements. The issue is therefore partially handled, not fully fixed.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the issue linked to PR #49996 and require the remaining lock/reboot/content-verification acceptance criteria to be demonstrated before closure.

evidence.fact: The issue contains detailed investigation and acceptance criteria for mixed-version installation.
Draft PR #49996 replaces custom manifest-driven copy/delete actions with MSI DuplicateFile authoring.
The issue states PR #49996 does not solve lock preflight, reliable reboot replacement, or post-install content verification.

fix_assessment.rationale: A linked draft PR addresses the normal replacement mechanism, while the explicitly documented acceptance gaps remain open.

issue_context.summary: Installing one PowerToys version over another can leave mixed-version files; a draft MSI change addresses part of the replacement mechanism but not all acceptance criteria.
known_information: PR #49996 is draft and not a complete resolution.
Controlled testing documented locked-file error/return-code cases and stale destination content.
The issue requires preflight, reboot replacement, and post-install verification behavior.
inferences: The remaining risk is installer state validation around locked files and reboot scheduling rather than only the copy authoring primitive.
issue_context.analysis: Track the draft PR against the full issue acceptance criteria and do not mark the bug fully resolved from the DuplicateFile change alone.

actions.label: Record partial installer fix
actions.note: Post the evidence-based status and linked public work.

comment.body: PR #49996 is the relevant existing work, but it should be treated as partial coverage only. The documented lock preflight, reliable reboot replacement, and post-install content verification requirements remain distinct from replacing custom copy/delete actions with MSI DuplicateFile authoring. Please keep those acceptance checks attached to the PR before considering this issue handled.
